slot_note: architecture 3, a re-root after architecture 2 (gas leak methane by district) was spent at the 11-01 re-check; it replaces shipped architecture 2 at ship
niche: a San Joaquin Valley farming company's water year 2026 groundwater extraction return to its subbasin's groundwater sustainability agency, integrated from the electric utility's interval data, the wells' pump efficiency tests, their water level transducers and the upper-aquifer wells' totalizer meters, and the transfer water it must buy before the agency's true-up
analyst_test: A strong analyst who conforms both utility exports, links every service agreement to its well through the pump test reports, reads the meters with their rollovers and replacements and converts each unmetered well's water year 2026 kilowatt-hours at its pump test's kilowatt-hours per acre-foot (which the metered upper-aquifer wells confirm within 2 per cent) files the ranch inside its allocation with no transfer to buy, while each hour's power converted at the head the pump lifted against that hour puts the lower-aquifer wells about 9 per cent higher and the ranch over its allocation.
domain_test: General statistics, so the swap is of the method: the deciding quantity is a data-integration estimate, each unmetered well's volume integrated from the utility's hourly energy and the well's own level record through its pump test, each hour's energy converted at the total head of that hour (the test's head moved by the gap between the hour's pumping level and the test's) at the test's overall efficiency; replacing it with a single-source summary (the test's kilowatt-hours per acre-foot, run hours times the tested flow, an average over tests) files the ranch inside its allocation.
layer1: the electric utility's interval data in two export layouts across its April 2026 portal change: hourly kWh in local prevailing time with duplicated and missing daylight-saving hours against 15-minute Wh in UTC, a meter exchange with a new multiplier, estimated intervals flagged

pump efficiency test reports from two testing contractors as PDFs, one giving total lift and total head, the other pumping level, discharge pressure in psi and total dynamic head, flow in gpm against acre-feet per 24 hours

water level transducer logs per well, vented loggers in depth to water below the measuring point and non-vented loggers in absolute pressure needing the ranch barologger, measuring points above ground surface by a stick-up recorded in the well register
totalizer meter reads on the upper-aquifer wells in acre-feet, thousands of gallons and gallons with six-digit rollovers and one meter replaced in June 2026
a well register naming wells by ranch name, state well number and the agency's well ID, with service agreement numbers renumbered at the utility's account migration
stakeholder_role: the ranch's water manager, who files its water year extraction return with the agency and arranges any transfer water before the true-up

spine.entity: one interval's energy on one well's electric service agreement

world.geography: United States (a fictional subbasin in California's San Joaquin Valley)
world.org_type: family-owned farming company growing pistachios and almonds on its own wells and district water

driver: The decisive quantity is a volume read through a metered input whose yield per unit of input is set by a physical state the meter does not see, measured once at one setting of that state; the state moves through the period and another system records it interval by interval, so the period's volume is each interval's input converted at its own state, and the single test's yield files the volume as if the state had stayed where the test found it.
driver_concrete: Each unmetered lower-aquifer well's water year 2026 extraction is each hour's kilowatt-hours times its pump test's overall efficiency over 1.0241 times the head the pump lifted against that hour, the test's total head moved by the gap between the hour's pumping level in the well's transducer log and the test's; the late-summer 2025 tests found the confined aquifer at its seasonal low, so their kilowatt-hours per acre-foot charge the spring and early-summer pumping, lifted 60 to 110 feet less, at the deep-season rate and file the ranch short of what it pumped.
stump: The default path converts each unmetered well's 2026 kilowatt-hours at its pump test's kilowatt-hours per acre-foot, which the metered upper-aquifer wells confirm within 2 per cent, and files the ranch inside its allocation with no transfer to buy, because it never asks what head each hour's power lifted water against.

differentiation.task140: task140 solves a reserved capacity tier together with a dependent service whose load rises with it; this build converts a metered energy record to water at each hour's own pumping head, a physical conversion with no reservation, tier or dependency

lineage.fate: spent at stage 4, 2026-10-20: judge SEND_BACK (Gate H rule_application) and both scored readers landed the call; the block-group rebuild was exact arithmetic once the area was filed
lineage.driver: A rate for an earlier period is needed for units drawn only later, and the units they were split from published it only as a whole, while finer units that tile the later units published it too; spreading the parent's rate to its parts makes the part holding the parent's high-rate pieces look like it rose and hides a rise in the other, so the earlier rate is rebuilt from the finer units and its error combined from theirs before the change is tested.
lineage.stump: The default path conforms the 2014 to 2018 tract estimates to 2020 tracts through the relationship file, gives each split tract's children their parent's poverty rate and margin of error, and designates Dunmore Heights and Linden Row, because the child holding a parent's poor block groups shows a significant rise that is only the split; rebuilding each child's earlier rate from its own 2010 block groups designates Dunmore Heights and Kestrel Park.

lineage.fate: spent 2026-11-01 at the re-check's stage 4: judge pass 4 NOT_DETERMINISTIC, SEND_BACK (Gate C/E underspecified_objective): guidelines 2.2 file a start only for called leaks, so a surveyed leak's start (find, previous survey, midpoint, seasonal expectation) designates 0, 12, 3 or 5 districts and nothing filed rules out the midpoint; the sentence that would close the fork names the decisive step, so the fork is the stump; the shipped pack stays at the portal, pending, untouched (target.zip 5a46ee5a)
lineage.driver: Each item is found only at a periodic inspection made at a fixed point in the year for each unit, after having begun at an unrecorded time since the previous inspection, and items begin mostly in one season, so the time each was active before it was found depends on when in the year its unit is inspected; the even-spread assumption misprices units inspected long after the season, and the seasonal profile comes from a second record whose items are reported as soon as they begin.
lineage.stump: The default path counts each 2026 leak's methane from the day it was found to its repair, and the textbook correction starts each surveyed leak halfway back to the previous survey; both designate the wrong districts, because leaks begin mostly in the frost months, so the districts surveyed in late autumn found leaks that had emitted since winter; estimating each leak's start from the monthly profile of the odor-report leaks designates the districts the program should fund.
lineage.niche: a city-owned gas utility's leak-based methane inventory by district for its accelerated cast-iron and bare-steel main replacement program, leaks found at once-a-year district surveys in each district's own month

notes: stump_strategy decomposition_attribution: each hour's metered energy is the product of the water lifted and the head it was lifted against, and the step splits it between them by the hour's own head; the field's energy-based method attributes the whole of it to water at the test's head.
